title: Mausoleum of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi, Turkistan
summary: A fired-brick Timurid mausoleum in Turkistan, southern Kazakhstan, built from 1389 to 1405 on Timur's order to replace a smaller 12th-century tomb. It stayed unfinished at his death, and its conic-spherical dome over the main hall is the largest in Central Asia.

uncertainty.note: UNESCO and ICOMOS both give 1389 to 1405; the building was never completed.

importance.justification: UNESCO World Heritage Site; one of the largest and best-preserved Timurid constructions and a prototype for later Timurid buildings in Samarkand.

phases.description: Built by order of Timur from 1389 to 1405 and left unfinished at his death (UNESCO, ICOMOS).
Stood unfinished, with the entrance and parts of the interior never completed; UNESCO notes neglect and inappropriate use in the mid-19th century.
ICOMOS records several restoration campaigns since 1945.
